newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Most Australia wheat pool prices up A$1.00/t.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Most Australia wheat pool prices up A$1.00/t.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said it had increased its 1996/97 pool price for most grades of wheat, including benchmark Australian Standard White (ASW), by A$1.00 a tonne.
This increases the ASW pool price to A$193.00 a tonne.
AWB general manager Ron Storey said noodle wheat prices were increased by A$6.00 to A$213.00 a tonne in Western Australia and by A$3.00 to A$205.00 a tonne in the eastern states.
Prices for feed wheat and the three durum grades are all unchanged.
Stiorey said the latest price rises, the third successive increase in pool equities, showed the AWB's marketing and shipping programmes remained on track.
"The general increase is a reflection of the continuing rapid early shipment pace," he said.
The noodle price rises reflected increased confidence in the AWB's sales programme for noodle wheat, which was sold to quality-conscious high-paying cusatomers, he said.
These customers bought consistently throughout the year. This meant that the noodle pool was more sensitive to fluctuating prices than other pools at the present time of year, he said.
The AWB did not mention its 1997/98 pool price in the statement. Two weeks ago, it said it intended to release the first 1997/98 pool returns estimate today.
